title: "🗓️ Session 10: Linear models in R"

date-modified: last-modified

This session implements the [lecture on regression analysis](/content/lecture/l_10_Regression.qmd)
in R. We work on **exactly the same data** as the lecture — 252 market research
analysts from the US Current Population Survey 2014 [@bekes2021data] — and
rebuild its models step by step, following the six steps of a regression
analysis (question, explore, specify, estimate, diagnose, interpret). More
precisely, we focus on the following topics:

- Fit simple and multiple linear regressions with `lm()` and present them in
  regression tables
- Reproduce the omitted variable bias formula from the lecture numerically
- Choose the functional form visually with `geom_smooth()`, and add quadratic
  and log terms
- Include categorical variables, set the reference category, and fit
  interaction models
- Plot predicted values to interpret nonlinear terms and interactions
- Produce and read diagnostic plots (Tukey-Anscombe plot, Q-Q plot)

The analysis of experimental data (t-tests, ANOVA, power analysis) follows in
[session 11](/content/material/s_11_Experiments.qmd), after the
[lecture on experiments](/content/lecture/l_11_Experiments.qmd).

## 👨‍🏫 Lecture Slides

There are no slides for this lab session. The relevant information is given
through the corresponding [lecture](/content/lecture/l_10_Regression.qmd) and
the mandatory readings.

## ✍️ Coursework

- Complete the in-class exercises at home
- Apply the six steps of a regression analysis to the data set `hr_salaries.csv`
  (in the [data sets of the mandatory reading](/content/material/data/RegressionDataSets.zip)):
  How are experience and education related to salaries — and does the return
  to experience differ by education? Write up your analysis as a short Quarto
  report.
- Do the exercises `LinearRegression1` and `LinearRegression2` from the `DataScienceExercises` package
